summary: Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his graduate studies under Leslie S. Kawamura at the University of Calgary, and he is attested as a professor at Simon Fraser University in 2010.

Paul David Numrich specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan by 1992, and held attested posts in 2006 at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at Collège de France (1946–1964), École Pratique des Hautes Études, Hōbōgirin, and the Institut de France.

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Christian Lassen at the University of Bonn and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a professor at the University of Kiel from circa 1889 to 1919.
Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he later served as a professor there from circa 1976 until 2017.

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (circa 1879–1883) and Ghent University (circa 1883–1920).
Paul Fuller is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rupert Gethin, and also studied under Paul Dundas.

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and studied at Columbia University. He held positions at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD from Yale University. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia, attested between 1982 and 2010.

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Münster, Mithila Research Institute, the University of Bonn, and the University of Pennsylvania.

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology who earned his PhD at the Australian National University. He held positions at ANU, the University of Canterbury, the University of Auckland, and Stanford University.

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He held academic posts at Chicago, Notre Dame, Wisconsin-Madison, Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.
Paul Kingsbury works in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona, attested in 2002.

Paul L. Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and studied at Otani University. In 1986, he held posts at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture.

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held academic posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1975–2006) and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and archaeology who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Jean Przyluski, and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at EPHE, Collège de France, and Yale University.
Paul Nietupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University, attested in 2008.

Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Édouard Chavannes and Émile Senart. He held positions at EFEO, Collège de France (1909, 1911–1945), and the Institut de France.

Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1869 to 1876 and held a post at the University of Lyon from circa 1879 to 1908.
Paul Rouzer is a scholar in the fields of sinology and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota (attested 2007).
